# <!--name-->Post Claude Review<!--/name-->

<!--description-->
Posts the review produced by claude-review as one PR comment (minimizing earlier ones) and, optionally, as a commit status. Run this in a job with pull-requests:write.
<!--/description-->

## Inputs

<!--inputs-->
| Name             | Description                                                                                   | Required | Default               |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|-----------------------|
| `review`         | The `review` output of claude-review. Empty means the review job produced nothing.            | `true`   | ` `                   |
| `github_token`   | GitHub token with pull-requests:write (and statuses:write when post_status is true).          | `false`  | `${{ github.token }}` |
| `post_status`    | Also publish a commit status on the PR head. success = a review was produced, failure = none. | `false`  | `false`               |
| `status_context` | Commit status context name.                                                                   | `false`  | `claude-review`       |
| `pr_number`      | Fallback PR number when `review` is empty (so a failure can still be reported on the PR).     | `false`  | ` `                   |
<!--/inputs-->

## Behaviour

- Earlier comments containing `<!-- claude-review -->` from bot accounts are minimized as outdated.
- Exactly one comment is posted per run. When the review job produced nothing, the comment says
  so and the step fails, so a silent review never reads as a clean one.
- Bodies over GitHub's limit are truncated with a link to the run.
- With `post_status: true`, the `claude-review` status is `success` when a review exists and
  `failure` otherwise. It never encodes approval.

## Example Usage

```yaml
- uses: mozilla/deploy-actions/claude-review/post@<sha>
  with:
    review: ${{ needs.review.outputs.review }}
    pr_number: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
    post_status: true
```
